So the reader cannot check the cited identity TP_sF_s=P_tF_tS, nor why the factor in D cancels the Gaussian weight at q_j, nor that (Nu)_j contains u_j exactly. These claims about a construction the page never states are not checkable.

gaps.quote: In $N=C\mathsf T\mathsf D$ the factor in $\mathsf D$ cancels the Gaussian weight at $q_j$, so $(Nu)_j$ contains $u_j$ exactly
gaps.note: Depends on the unstated definition of T (sum of exp(-pi alpha^2 (tj/s-k)^2) u_j); without it the reader cannot verify the cancellation or that the remaining summands form (N-I)u.

gaps.quote: The resampling reduces $F_s$ to a power-of-two $F_t$, which is a [Multidimensional transforms](multidim-transform.md) over short axes.
gaps.note: The stated hypotheses (and the paper's Lemma, line 3550) only require integers 2<=s<t<2^p with gcd(s,t)=1 and theta>p/alpha^4; t is not required to be a power of two, and s is not required to be prime, although the intro says 'prime length s' and 'power-of-two length t'. The claim that F_t is a multidimensional transform over short axes is not derived on this page; it is a later step in the paper, not part of this lemma.

gaps.quote: Contraction of the exact maps yields errors less than $16p<p^2$ and $4+3p^2/4<p^2$
gaps.note: The inequalities 16p<p^2 and 4+3p^2/4<p^2 need p>16; the paper's lemma assumes p>100 (line 3550), which the page omits when stating the hypotheses (it only says s<t<2^p and 2<=alpha<sqrt p). Without p>100 (also needed for the cited Lemma 2.12) the claim is false for small p. Also the page never defines 'error' of an approximation (paper lines 3529-3534: 2^p||L~u-Lu||<E) nor the rule that errors of composed maps add, so the reader cannot check where 16p and 4+3p^2/4 come from.

gaps.term: bound on E-tilde needs z in D_p
gaps.note: The paper states this only for z in D_p^s (lines 3750-3757), where ||z||<=1. As written for arbitrary z the final '<1' is false (take z large). The page also does not say what E-tilde is or that it comes from Lemma 4.11 of the cited paper.
